note: Copy for the US testing guide (/us/tests/). Every fact here comes from src/data/us/tests.json (verified October 12, 2026). 'src' points at a source in that file: [section, a piece of the source label]. 'hud' is the small label drawn on the photo; keep it a real measurement convention.

groups.title: Home health
groups.intro: A standard energy audit doesn't cover these. Each has its own federal guidance and, in many states, its own license or certification.

groups.title: Energy performance
groups.intro: These measure how your home uses and loses energy. DOE says many professional assessments include a blower door test and an infrared scan; ask for the others by name.

tests.name: Radon test
tests.why: EPA recommends fixing a home at 4 pCi/L or more and says every home should be tested, whatever its radon zone.
tests.who: You, with a short-term kit, or an NRPP- or NRSB-certified pro (state-licensed where required)

tests.name: Carbon monoxide alarms
tests.why: CPSC recommends a CO alarm on every level and outside sleeping areas. Most of the states we checked also require alarms in at least some homes.
tests.who: You install the alarms; auditors check CO in the air during an audit

tests.name: Lead paint testing
tests.why: Homes built before 1978 are more likely to have lead-based paint. Most paid work that disturbs paint in these homes must be done by a lead-safe certified firm.
src: Protect Your Family from Sources of Lead
tests.who: EPA- or state-certified inspectors and risk assessors; lead-safe certified firms for renovation

tests.name: Asbestos & vermiculite
tests.why: More than 70% of the vermiculite sold in the U.S. from 1919 to 1990 came from a Libby, Montana mine contaminated with asbestos. Leave it alone and use accredited pros.
tests.who: Trained, accredited asbestos professionals; your state agency says who may work there

tests.name: Mold & indoor air
tests.why: There are no federal limits for mold, so sampling can't show a pass or fail. Fixing the water problem is the job.
tests.fact: DIY cleanup: under about 10 sq ft
tests.who: You, for small areas; licensed assessors and remediators in some states

tests.name: Well water testing
tests.why: Private wells fall outside the Safe Drinking Water Act. EPA says to test every year for coliform bacteria, nitrates, total dissolved solids and pH.
tests.who: A lab certified for drinking-water testing; some local health departments test for free

tests.name: Blower door test
tests.why: Measures whole-house air leakage at 50 pascals. The 2021 IECC caps new homes at 5.0 ACH50 in climate zones 0–2 and 3.0 ACH50 in zones 3–8.
tests.who: Energy auditors and RESNET HERS raters

tests.name: Infrared (thermal) scan
tests.why: An infrared camera finds missing insulation and air leaks. ASTM's leak-detection practice says to pressurize or depressurize the house so the leaks show up.
tests.who: Energy auditors, ideally while the blower door holds the house under pressure

tests.name: Manual J load calculation
tests.why: ACCA's ANSI-recognized method for a home's heating and cooling loads. Where the IECC or IRC is adopted, equipment must be sized per Manual S from Manual J loads, or another approved method.
tests.fact: ACCA Manual J, S and D
tests.who: Whoever sizes your heating and cooling equipment

tests.name: Duct leakage test
tests.why: Pressure-tests the ductwork at 25 pascals. The 2021 IECC allows new homes up to 4.0 CFM25 of total leakage per 100 sq ft of conditioned floor area.
tests.who: Energy auditors and RESNET HERS raters

tests.name: Combustion safety test
tests.why: Checks furnaces, boilers and water heaters for spillage and carbon monoxide under worst-case conditions. DOE calls for it in homes with natural-draft appliances, especially during air sealing.

tests.name: Attic insulation check
tests.why: ENERGY STAR recommends R30 to R60 for an uninsulated attic, depending on your climate zone.
tests.who: You can check the depth; an auditor can check the rest

tests.name: Utility bill analysis
tests.why: Your past bills are what savings predictions get calibrated to (BPI-2400). Green Button lets you download your usage if your utility supports it.
tests.who: You, with your utility’s data, and your auditor
